stem: Brightline Logistics wants a different state bucket per environment, taken from an input variable, and is also trialing HCP Terraform workspaces from the same configuration. Which statement about what Terraform allows is accurate?

choices.text: A backend block cannot reference an input variable, and a cloud block cannot share a configuration with a backend block
A backend block can reference an input variable, though not locals or data source attributes in the same configuration
A configuration can declare one backend block per environment and select among them with named workspaces at init time
A cloud block can sit beside a backend block, so state is written to both places

rationale: A backend block cannot refer to named values such as input variables, locals or data source attributes, so a variable-driven bucket name is not possible there (partial configuration is the workaround). A configuration can provide only one backend block, and a configuration with a cloud block cannot include a backend block, because HCP Terraform manages state in its own workspaces. Workspaces do not change the one-block rule, so a cloud block cannot sit beside a backend block.
